s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of headache and diplopia with cranial nerve palsies
salient_findings: Right cranial nerve VI and III palsies
key_facts: 70-year-old man
Medical history of atrial fibrillation
Sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker placement
Prostate cancer treated with radiation and hormonal therapy
Obstructive sleep apnea
Left-sided Bell's palsy
Tobacco misuse
Preexisting left-sided incomplete facial nerve palsy
Visual acuity and peripheral vision intact bilaterally
Severe photosensitivity
Normal funduscopic examination
Air fluid levels in bilateral sphenoid and maxillary sinuses on CTA
Irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI
Left pleural effusion on CT thorax
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT thorax
Mass-like thickening of the posterior left pleura on CT thorax
Mesenteric lymphadenopathy on CT abdomen and pelvis

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of headache and diplopia with cranial nerve palsies, irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI, lymphadenopathy on CT scans, and history of prostate cancer

shortlist.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of prostate cancer, mass-like thickening of the posterior left pleura on CT thorax, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphadenopathy on CT scans, biopsy of posterior left pleural thickening showed CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type

shortlist.label: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Air fluid levels in bilateral sphenoid and maxillary sinuses on CTA, and mass-like thickening of the posterior left pleura on CT thorax

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus and lymphadenopathy in multiple regions, along with the biopsy results showing CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type, are consistent with lymphoma.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: While it could explain the cranial nerve palsies, it doesn't account for the systemic findings like mediastinal and mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a type of lymphoma, but the systemic involvement suggests a more widespread disease, not limited to the cavernous sinus.

rejected.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
rejected.why: The biopsy of the posterior left pleural thickening did not show prostate cancer cells, and the patient's prostate cancer was treated with radiation and hormonal therapy, making metastasis less likely.

rejected.label: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma
rejected.why: There's no direct evidence provided in the case that points to nasopharyngeal carcinoma, such as a mass in the nasopharynx or specific symptoms related to this condition.
